name: Graph theory: networks
description: Vertices, edges, trees, routes, colourings, flows and counting networks, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about:
Graph theory realm ("Graph theory: networks"): vertices, edges, trees, routes, colourings, matchings, flows and exact counting, for an
adult who has finished Foundations and Discrete mathematics. Same Kepler outpost, now linked up: the Map Room plans every tunnel, cable,
road and pipe between the domes, and Mira is still the mentor. The concept plan is docs/plans/GRAPH-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Points and links
chapters.blurb: Vertices, edges, degrees, complete graphs, complements, isomorphism and walks.

sector.name: Map Room
sector.purpose: draw every link between the domes

chapters.name: Getting around
chapters.blurb: Distance, components, Euler circuits and trails, and eulerising a road map.

sector.name: Rover Depot
sector.purpose: drive every road without doubling back

chapters.name: Trees
chapters.blurb: Trees, leaves, forests, spanning trees and Kruskal's algorithm.

sector.name: Cable Yard
sector.purpose: connect every dome with the least cable

chapters.name: Routes and tours
chapters.blurb: Shortest paths, Hamilton cycles, the travelling salesperson and Dirac's theorem.

sector.name: Dispatch
sector.purpose: plan the shortest tour of the outlying stations

chapters.name: Planarity and colouring
chapters.blurb: Euler's formula, planar limits, polyhedra, bipartite graphs and colouring.

sector.name: Circuit Shop
sector.purpose: lay out circuits whose wires never cross

chapters.name: Matching and flow
chapters.blurb: Matchings, Hall's condition, directed paths, flows and cuts.

sector.name: Pumping Station
sector.purpose: push as much water as the pipes allow

chapters.name: Counting structures
chapters.blurb: Labelled trees, Prüfer codes, cliques, triangles and Ramsey's guarantee.

sector.name: Archive
sector.purpose: count every network we could ever build

source.label: OpenStax and Keller and Trotter

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. The domes are linked by a tangle of tunnels and cables, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have everything this needs from Foundations and Discrete mathematics. I’ll work the first example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Every dome needs a link.
Learn the shape of a network.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Map Room. The outpost is now a scatter of domes, and every tunnel, cable and road between them is a line on this table. We start by counting the links we already have.
copy.allDone: Every road, cable and pipe at the outpost is now planned on paper first. Topology opens next in the Survey Grid, where a network becomes a shape.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from vertices and edges to trees and flows. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the answer before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Draw the links before you count them.
help.intro: Graph theory starts where Discrete mathematics ends: with the links between things. It teaches how to describe, route, colour and count networks exactly, without drawing every case. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Answers are whole numbers, such as a count, a weight or a degree, never a route or a list of edges. Type them without commas or spaces (1250, not 1,250). A yes or no is typed as 1 or 0, and a dome is typed by its number.
